must_remember: Brewster's law states that the tangent of the polarizing angle equals the relative refractive index of the medium: $\tan(i_p) = \mu_{21}$.
At Brewster's angle, the reflected and refracted rays are mutually perpendicular, meaning $i_p + r = 90^\circ$.
The reflected light at Brewster's angle is 100% plane-polarized with electric field oscillations perpendicular to the plane of incidence.
The refracted ray is only partially polarized because it retains both parallel and perpendicular polarization components.
Brewster's law is applicable to any transparent dielectric interface, not just air-to-medium boundaries.

glossary.meaning: The angle of incidence at which reflected light is completely plane-polarized parallel to the reflecting surface.
The physical law stating that $\tan(i_p) = \mu$, linking the refractive index to the polarizing angle.
The plane containing the incident ray, the normal to the interface, the reflected ray, and the refracted ray.
The ratio of the refractive index of medium 2 to that of medium 1, expressed as $\mu_2 / \mu_1$.
